title: yargs-parser
standardAlternative: util.parseArgs from node:util parses typed long and short options, though without dot-notation, camel-case aliases, counts or coercion.
notes: test/yargs-parser.mjs and test/string-utils.mjs run unchanged under mocha 11.8.0 with chai 5.3.3, the versions upstream's devDependencies resolve to. They import ../build/lib/index.js and ../build/lib/string-utils.js; the aliases point those at shims/index.mjs (the subject's default export) and shims/string-utils.mjs, which exposes camelCase, decamelize and looksLikeNumber from the subject's parser helpers, so the module ships the helpers on the parser instead of as a second file.

The Create API is yargs-parser's default export with parser.detailed, parser.camelCase, parser.decamelize and parser.looksLikeNumber. It leaves out configuration files (opts.config), opts.configObjects, environment variables (opts.envPrefix), the combine-arrays flag (which only merges those sources), opts.key and the opts.__ translation hook; the Configuration type keeps the other 17 flags. The spec states the subset.

Fuzz outputs are compared with object keys sorted, because yargs-parser's key order depends on insertion details the spec does not pin down; the alias lists of parser.detailed are sorted too. Generated argv names normalize at most once, as --path P or --path=P, so path.normalize stays on POSIX-style inputs.

Feature selectors list exact test titles. '#' is dropped from titles, because mocha's TAP reporter cuts a test name at '#' ("should handle parsing negative #s" becomes "should handle parsing negative s").
